items.title: East German vocabulary after 1990
items.claim: After German reunification (1990), East German specific vocabulary largely faded. One word that survived in widespread use is:
items.reveal_title: The Ampelmannchen survived as a cultural icon
items.reveal:
Created in 1961 by Karl Peglau, the East Berlin pedestrian-light figure was retained after unification following public campaigns.

Most specifically DDR-era political vocabulary disappeared from active use within a decade.
items.why: Symbols can outlive the political contexts that created them.

items.title: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt
items.claim: Bertolt Brecht's theatre theory is widely translated as 'alienation effect'. What does Verfremdungseffekt specifically aim to do?

options.text: Make audiences identify completely with characters
Disrupt emotional immersion so the audience thinks critically about the social conditions depicted
Make plays as short as possible

items.reveal:
Brecht developed the concept from the late 1920s. Verfremdung is closer to 'making strange' than to ordinary alienation.

The Berliner Ensemble, founded with Helene Weigel in 1949, became its main institutional home.
items.why: Translation choices can shift the apparent meaning of a theoretical term.

items.title: The longest German word in use
items.claim: German allows long noun compounds. A famous legal-administrative example abolished in 2013 was:
items.reveal:
The cattle-marking-and-beef-labelling-supervision-duties-delegation-law was repealed in 2013, partially because EU rules changed.

The Duden does not generally treat such legal compounds as 'words' for dictionary purposes.
items.why: Morphological possibility is not the same as everyday usage.
